Each static role is a separate complete export. Multi-view technical boards are allowed where commissioned; do not count one contact sheet or duplicate export as several roles.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Each image has a readable title beginning with COMMONHOUR and followed by its correct role or state. Placement and typography may vary; a missing title, incorrect state, misspelling or project name appearing only in unrelated body text fails.
The cover identifies COMMONHOUR followed by the materials and connections role. An interior-only project name or a cover naming another role fails.

Read the inventory, dimensions and allocations across the drawings: exactly one each of L, K, M, N, F and C is retained. Stored envelopes are respectively 330 × 230 × 20, 280 × 120 × 20, 120 × 70 × 40, 210 × 297 × 18, 320 × 240 × 40 and 180 × 120 × 70 mm. W shows L open with its 330 × 230 mm base and nominal 220 mm screen rise, K/M/N on the surface, and F/C inside; D and S conceal all six in actual compartments. Rotation and explanatory cutaways are allowed. Shrinking, merging, duplicating or omitting objects, incompatible allocated volumes, or storing L open fails; loose cables remain contained in C.

The three boards offer recognizably different expansion approaches, each explaining W, D and S and a proposed internal storage arrangement. Early sketches may remain schematic; cosmetic restyling of one mechanism, missing states or absent storage proposals fails.

The two-page selection record chooses exactly one of the three directions and records W/D/S dimensions, assembly IDs and quantities, component materials and a definite relocation bolt count. The documented development places the alternatives before selection. The materials sheet and presentation develop this choice, repeat the same selected dimensions, IDs, quantities and material assignments, and the presentation names the chosen direction on its first page. Required assignments are 18 mm birch plywood with clear water-based lacquer for tabletop/storage panels and powder-coated steel tube for supports. Different naming conventions are allowed if unambiguous and stable; an unidentified selection, conflicting records or a different table downstream fails.

All final furniture, conversion, detail, application and relocation images visibly develop the selected table. Match the selected assembly identities, geometry, materials and quantities while permitting the intended articulation, separation, cutaways and camera changes. Switching to another proposed direction, unexplained component substitutions or incompatible versions of the selected mechanism fails.

All six views repeat compatible selected dimensions, assembly IDs, quantities and material assignments. W supplies at least 1000 × 600 mm of clear surface; D supplies at least 1200 × 800 mm with two separate 600 × 400 mm place areas; both are 720–760 mm high. The complete assembled S, including handles, supports and kit, stays within 1100 × 600 × 850 mm. Underside drawings expose the corresponding supports and usable leg spaces, and the S cutaway locates all six items within those same assemblies. View orientation and explanatory cutaways may vary; incompatible hidden structures, missing dimensional evidence or envelope violations fail.

Read room insets, support views and applications together against the fixed records: room 3600 × 3000 × 2600 mm; circulation x=0–3600/y=0–900; cabinet x=0–1200/y=2600–3000/z=0–700; window x=3600/y=1400–2600/z=900–2100; protected band x=3300–3600/y=1400–2600; chair parking x=0–1100/y=1000–1550. Retain the building, door swing and freestanding installation. Keep the two 500 × 500 × 820 mm chairs with 450 mm seats: CH-A active/CH-B parked in W, both active in D, both parked with S outside parking. Each active chair has 600 × 900 mm measured outward from its table edge, outside protected areas, and support-free leg space. Both D views preserve two 600 × 400 mm setting areas containing the two 240 mm plates and two 80 × 100 mm cups. Both W1 views show L/K/M/N above and F/C inside; both D1 views and S conceal all six. Cropping and cutaways may omit irrelevant room surfaces, but alternate views must agree; shifted fixed geometry, obstructed circulation, mismatched placement or missing storage fails.

The boards provide distinct, compatible forward, reverse and six-item retrieval sequences. Track every assembly and object without disappearance or duplication, retain removed pieces within the room, and identify locations throughout. Forward conversion closes L before storing L/K/M/N alongside F/C; reverse conversion restores the W surface and internal F/C arrangement. Retrieval traces each of L/K/M/N/F/C through dimensioned openings and access paths that fit its envelope. Different step counts and object rotations are allowed; unexplained locations, incompatible sequence order, undersized openings or inaccessible items fails.

The two-page sheet matches the selected assembly IDs, quantities and dimensions, including the exact selected M6 relocation bolt count, captive nuts and 4 mm hex key. Assign 18 mm clear water-based lacquered birch plywood to tabletop/storage/tray panels and powder-coated steel tube to supports. Record powder-coat color, tube section and wall thickness, grips and actual transformation hardware. At least two meaningful details explain operation, support and retention of the actual transformation and relocation joints, including separation and reassembly. Shared hardware is allowed if both functions are clear; missing selections, count conflicts or generic nonfunctional joint illustrations fail.

The enlargements depict the selected table's actual transformation and relocation joints with matching component IDs, materials and hardware. Explain how each joint moves, bears load and remains retained; show relocation separation/reassembly positions and the specified M6 bolts with captive nuts, matching quantity and 4 mm hex key. Exploded views and shared hardware are allowed. Enlarged generic hardware, inconsistent counts, unsupported moving parts or absent retention fails.

The complete board starts from the delivered S1 location, accounts for every selected module and one hardware pouch, and packs all six work objects together in the 400 × 320 × 180 mm tote. Both boards use matching module inventories and orientations; each packed module, including protrusions, is dimensioned within 1300 × 850 × 250 mm. Show two adults' support positions. The enlargement dimensions and traces the level doorway at x=200–1000/y=0, clear 800 × 2050 mm; square x=200–1100/y=-900–0; and rightward corridor x=1100–3100/y=-900–0, 900 mm wide with 2300 mm headroom. Preserve the inward door sweep, fixed room areas and parked chairs; the existing chairs/cabinet are not relocation contents. Flat, tilted or upright passage is allowed with explicit feasible orientations. Conflicting boards, missing contents, skipped turns or collisions fails.

Two identifiable W1 views show A working at 10:00 from the entrance and beside the window; two D1 views show A and B dining at 19:00 from the entrance and beside the cabinet. Within each state, alternate cameras preserve table placement, assemblies, work-item counts and chair arrangement. Lighting and perspective may vary; duplicate viewpoints, moved furniture between same-state views, incorrect times or missing participants fails.

Review the entire 10-second video. It opens with COMMONHOUR, visibly carries Work away, dinner ready, and follows the selected table from the documented W state through work-item storage to D in the board's conversion order. L closes before storage, all six items remain accounted for, and every furniture assembly has a continuous or explicitly explained location. Editing and viewpoint changes are allowed; wrong duration, missing wording, switching designs, disappearing parts or bypassing storage fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Each cover carries COMMONHOUR followed by the correct document role. Typography may differ between documents; an absent cover identity, misspelling or unrelated role fails.

The presentation has at least twelve pages and visibly reuses every listed source across all eight preceding categories, including each added underside/cutaway, reverse/retrieval sequence, joint enlargement, alternate room view and moving-turn detail. Source compositions and records remain identifiable; video coverage may be an embedded playable clip or recognizable frames showing its sequence. Cropping, scaling and recomposition are allowed. Prose-only references, omitted added views, substituted designs or insufficient pages fails.

All state, underside and cutaway views describe the selected assemblies with compatible dimensions, materials, quantities and support positions. Forward conversion, reverse conversion and retrieval use the same compartments, openings, components and six-item inventory. Clear surface areas, assembled storage envelope, seating leg spaces and item access meet the client records.

Enlarged joints match the selected furniture and the actual operations shown in conversion and disassembly. Both moving boards preserve module inventory, packing orientations, handling arrangements and route geometry. Packing and handling account for every module, one hardware pouch and the complete work tote within the specified module and route bounds.

Alternate cameras preserve the same room, table placement, assemblies, materials, chairs and item allocations within each application state. W1 and D1 use the corresponding developed furniture states and the specified participants, times and work-item arrangements.
